key_insight: A self-supervised CT foundation model (CIPHER) can predict which lung cancer patients are more likely to develop immune checkpoint inhibitor–induced pneumonitis before treatment starts.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this could help clinicians identify higher-risk patients for closer monitoring and earlier intervention during immunotherapy.
method: Pretrained on 590,284 CT slices from 2,500 NSCLC patients using contrastive learning plus a transformer-based masked autoencoder.
Fine-tuned on an internal immunotherapy cohort while using only non-pneumonitis cases for training and reserving a held-out validation set with adjudicated ICI-P cases.
Benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and ensemble models, then tested in an independent external NSCLC cohort.
evidence_signal: CIPHER achieved AUCs of 0.77-0.85 internally, AUC 0.83 in head-to-head benchmarking, and AUC 0.83 with 81.7% balanced accuracy in external validation.
watch_item: This is a retrospective imaging model, so broader prospective validation and workflow integration are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: CT-Based Deep Foundation Model for Predicting Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Pneumonitis Risk in Lung Cancer
